newsitem.title: UK: Zenith Media cites threat from Disney-style giants.
newsitem.headline: Zenith Media cites threat from Disney-style giants.

text.p: Global entertainment and media owners pose a threat to advertising agencies and media-buying specialists, John Perris, chairman of Zenith Media, said on Thursday.
Perris told a business conference that global media companies, which he described as "communiglomerates", were offering integrated media packages that enabled advertisers to bypass ad agencies.
He told a conference called "The Emperor's New Clothes: Ten Media Myths Exploded" that Walt Disney Co was the kind of "communiglomerate" to watch for.

"Apart from the films that we are all familiar with, they (Disney) own amongst other things, the ABC TV network in the U.s. and several radio stations, they are into publishing and videos, own theme parks and cruise ships.

"They offer advertisers not only media air time, but can also take those advertisers into cinemas, theme parks and cruise ships," said Perris, whose Zenith Media is the media-buying arm of Cordiant Plc, which owns Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising.
"If, for example, you are a fast food or soft drink company, not only can you advertise on ABC but you also get a franchise at a Disney theme park," he said.
Perris said that General Motors Corp and Macdonald's had both done tie-ups with Disney in the United States.

"In Macdonald's the paper tray liner featured ABC's autumn programme schedule and Macdonald's in turn advertised on ABC. You can start to see how easy it is for them to orchestrate this for advertisers. It is a frightening scenario for ad agencies," he said.
However, he said that while this was a growing trend in the U.S., the situation in Europe was different.
"I think Europe will be slow to adopt it. European media owners are too small to compete on a global scale," Perris said.

At the same conference Martin Sorrell, chief executive of WPP Group Plc, the world's biggest marketing services company, said that there were opportunities for advertising agencies and media buyers to work with the new media "communiglomerates".
Media buyers are groups that deal with television companies and other media owners to book television airtime or other advertising space on behalf of advertisers and ad agencies.

Sorrell said WPP, which owns J.Walter Thompson, Ogilvy & Mather and several other global agencies, bought up a significant proportion of advertising space in India, which was an important growth market for its clients.

He said global ad agencies had expertise and market share that could help "communiglomerates" in emerging markets such as India, while the huge entertainment and media groups could help ad agencies in the West.
"They can help us in mature markets and we can help them in emerging markets such as India," he said.
Thursday's conference was organised by Haymarket Conferences, the conference division linked to Campaign and Marketing magazines.
